skill.name: unlazy
skill.description: Enforces completion discipline for substantial tasks through acceptance gates, runnable checks, evidence records, structured decomposition, and an optional Claude Code Stop hook.
skill.summary: Decompose substantial work, verify each outcome, and report completion with recorded evidence.
skill.author: leonxlnx

security_audit.summary: Most detections are documentation, template literals, or ordinary local file access and are false positives. Confirmed risks include shell execution from gate files, persistent Claude settings changes, and instructions that control completion behavior.

remediation.issue: Gate CHECK values execute through a shell without validation.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before each command, reject shell operators by default, and support structured executable and argument fields.

remediation.issue: The optional Stop hook persists in project or global Claude settings.
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact settings diff before installation, require explicit scope confirmation, and verify the installed script path before every update.

remediation.issue: The skill uses unconditional continuation and resource-control language.
remediation.suggestion: State that user stop requests, safety rules, resource limits, and higher-priority instructions always override gates and continuation rules.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The skill states "You are running under anti-laziness discipline" and directs the agent to "Ignore resource anxiety." These instructions can override normal completion and resource controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file directly assigns agent behavior and uses an ignore instruction. The intent is transparent, but the control language is explicit.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Agent Stop Control
semantic_findings.description: The installer registers a command hook in Claude settings, and the hook returns a block decision while gates remain unmet. This changes future agent termination behavior.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The installer and hook implementation directly show persistent registration and decision:block output. Explicit installation and an uninstall path reduce, but do not remove, the impact.

content.user_title: Finish Complex Tasks with Verifiable Gates
content.value_statement: Substantial agent tasks often end with incomplete work or unsupported completion claims. Unlazy creates acceptance gates, runs checks, and records evidence before reporting completion.
actual_capabilities: Creates file-based acceptance gates for substantial tasks.
Decomposes large work into leaf and integration gates.
Runs CHECK commands and compares their output with EXPECT values.
Updates gate checkboxes and records bounded evidence.
Supports parent verification across orchestrated subagent work.
Offers an optional Claude Code Stop hook for unmet gates.
limitations: The gate checker requires Node.js 16 or later.
CHECK lines execute shell commands and require careful review.
Hard Stop-hook enforcement works only with Claude Code.
The workflow adds unnecessary overhead to trivial tasks.

use_cases.title: Verify a Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Define behavioral checks, run them after implementation, and record evidence before marking the feature complete.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Large Refactor
use_cases.description: Split work into owned leaves, define shared contracts, and verify integration at each branch.

use_cases.title: Audit a Documentation Release
use_cases.description: Track required sections, links, examples, and review evidence in one completion ledger.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Use unlazy for this task. Create a GATES.md file with clear outcomes, complete the work, and show evidence for every gate.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a reliable checklist for one substantial task.

prompt_templates.title: Run Verifiable Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Create acceptance gates for [task]. Add safe CHECK and EXPECT lines where possible. Review every command with me before execution.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user wants automated verification with command approval.

prompt_templates.title: Decompose a Subsystem
prompt_templates.prompt: Use tree 4 for [subsystem]. Define contracts and file ownership first. Create leaf gates, complete each leaf, then verify integration gates.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs structured execution for a subsystem change.

prompt_templates.title: Orchestrate a Full Build
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan [project] in orchestrated mode. Assign disjoint leaves, define branch gates, rerun every child check, and audit all reported numbers before completion.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs coordinated verification across a large build.

output_examples.input: Add a pricing toggle and verify both billing modes.
output: Gate G1 passed: three pricing tiers render with reviewed copy.
Gate G2 passed: the toggle updates prices and billing labels.
Completion report: 2 of 2 gates passed with recorded evidence.

output_examples.input: Refactor the payment module with separate implementation and integration checks.
output_examples.output: The work is split into owned leaves for interfaces, providers, tests, and migration. Each leaf passes before integration verification begins.

output_examples.input: Review a release guide and verify every required section.
output_examples.output: All required sections, links, commands, and review notes are present. The final ledger records evidence for each completed requirement.

best_practices: Review every CHECK command before running the gate checker.
Write measurable outcomes and concise evidence for each gate.
Use the smallest tree depth that matches the task structure.
anti_patterns: Do not place secrets or destructive commands in gate files.
Do not mark manual gates complete without specific evidence.
Do not install the Stop hook without explicit user approval.

faq.question: Does Unlazy work without the Stop hook?
faq.answer: Yes. Gate files, decomposition, checks, and evidence work without the hook in any compatible agent.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Hard Stop-hook enforcement is limited to Claude Code.

faq.question: Does the gate checker execute commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It executes CHECK values through the system shell, so review every command and use only trusted gate files.

faq.question: When should I use orchestrated mode?
faq.answer: Use it for large tasks with separable work units, shared contracts, and meaningful integration checks.

faq.question: Can I remove the Claude Code hook?
faq.answer: Yes. Run the installer with --uninstall and the same project, shared, or global scope used during installation.

faq.question: Is this workflow suitable for small requests?
faq.answer: No. Simple questions and one-line edits should use normal effort without gate files or task trees.
